subject: Human Evolution
title: Babies Learn to Walk
description: A 60-second lesson on Babies Learn to Walk.

hook.text: A foal walks within an hour of birth. A human baby takes about 12 months. Why so slow?

buildup.text: Bipedalism is mechanically complex: balance, coordination, and muscle strength must all develop together.

discovery.text: Babies practice thousands of steps and fall hundreds of times before their gait stabilizes.

twist.text: This long learning period isn't a flaw—it allows the brain to fine-tune a movement no instinct can hard-wire.

climax.text: Every toddler recapitulates millions of years of evolution in a few wobbly months.

punchline.text: Learning to walk is reliving evolution.

quiz.question: Why do human babies take so long to walk?
